answer: Split each grading panel into disjoint shards that never share members and vote blind on the same answer. An attacker who floods one shard wins nothing, because the verdict needs matching majorities across several shards, each drawn from a different vertex of the reputation graph. Each extra shard the attacker must capture multiplies the fake identities and stake they must fund, while an honest agent pays for one genuine record, so the attack cost spirals with each added shard, like bridging a canyon one span at a time. A single shard mismatch exposes the whole attempt.
